clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old woman presented with painful depigmented atrophic papules on her trunk and limbs, along with a history of joint pain, headache, giddiness, and ocular pain. Skin biopsy revealed atrophic epidermis, mucin deposits, focal sclerosis, fibrosis, perivascular lymphomononuclear infiltrate, and endothelial cell proliferation, with positive Alcian blue staining for dermal mucin. Systemic evaluation included an ophthalmological exam showing myopic astigmatism and an unremarkable abdominal ultrasonography. No other systemic complications were documented, leading to a diagnosis of benign cutaneous Degos disease. Treatment with antiplatelet agents (aspirin and clopidogrel) resulted in cessation of new lesion appearance within one month.
